Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
Changeling-alpha: 40. The movable cells fill about 30 % of the area outside the macros. With 60 the placer packed them
densely and routing did not converge on the three routing layers below the power stripes (Metal3 overflow, run 45008997433).
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz. Changeling-alpha is specified for 60 MHz.
Timing repair during place and route works on the default corner. With the typical corner it found nothing to
repair while the slow corner failed by 9.6 ns (run 45045076268), so the slow corner is the default corner here.
Constraints of the flow plus the two-cycle exception for the instruction paths of the cores (see the file).
IHP_CELLS: rsoc8/rtl/rlinecells.v instantiates the library clock gate sg13cmos5l_lgcp_1.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
======== IHP SRAM macros: three RM_IHPSG13_1P_1024x16_c2_bm_bist (code memory of core 0 and core 1, data memory) ========
This section follows the Tiny Tapeout example ttcodebot/ttihp-cmos5l-sram-example (after Ken Pettit's CMOS5L SRAM design).
Insert the Project.ExtendPowerStripes step (librelane_plugin_sram_pdn.py) after the PDN generator.
Macro views straight from the PDK (sg13cmos5l_sram is a link to sg13g2_sram).
A macro is 236.8 x 336.46 um; the 8x4 project area is 1724.16 x 710.64 um. The three instances stand side by side
at the bottom left, flipped (FS) so that their pins face up towards the logic. x = 3.36 + n x 11.24 um keeps the power
columns of every macro under the PDN stripes (n = 0, 53, 106). The macros are spread over the width, so that their
pins are not all in one corner (routing did not converge with the macros side by side, run 45032707393). A gap
between macros has to be either inside the macro halos or wide enough for power stripes (PDN-0179 otherwise).
Instance names: hierarchy below the top module.
The SRAM has two supply rails (VDD!, VDDARRAY!) and one ground rail (VSS!).
PDN: Skip connecting the SRAM by pdngen; it is powered by ExtendPowerStripes instead.
Optional: extra power stripe pairs over the SRAM's bit-cell arrays, for better power delivery to the macro.
pdngen checks the SRAM's power connections before ExtendPowerStripes makes them, so errors are expected at this stage.
Magic DRC flags many errors inside the SRAM macro (seen in the SG13G2 SRAM projects).
The Tiny Tapeout precheck runs the full KLayout DRC deck on the final GDS instead.
Magic extracts the SRAM from its LEF abstract, so the power stripes crossing the macro's
Metal4 obstruction show up as illegal overlaps (there is no metal there in the GDS).
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html
